title: Dupree as family friend and early gigs together
summary: How Dupree knew the family, other pianists like Toots Washington, and going out as a youngster to play for pay.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Were you related to Dupree too?
Well, not blood, just at my house so much he'd always say we were family. You know, like I said you're my cousin, you know, because he'd come visit you so much.
Well how did he know your family?

Well he knew my mother and them before he knew me. He knew my sisters, he knew my brothers. They knew him so long ago. I don't remember when they met. Like I said, it's like I know people in New Orleans. We've just been friends. So long I can't just say, okay one day I was on the corner and he came up. He was always there. And he would play the piano and all the neighbors would come. Miss Gordon always had something going on musically at the house. Nobody played music. But the piano was there.
Well I must have been experienced to listen to Champion Jack.

I sit right there and listen to all of it. Not only him, Toots Washington used to stop by. Toots? Yeah, Papa Yellow. Yeah, he touched. Yeah, that was my man, God bless him. And all of these guys, like I said, they had a smile and lures. I was very young and these guys would come and get me and it was an experience. And they all tell my mother, they'd take care of me. We used to go like the slide out, we'd make three dollars, five dollars for that night. Not be a child, you know, with these men. But they would all bring me home. They'd pay me just like they paid the other guys.
You would go with Champion Jack? Yeah, I would go with Jack.
It was really like the slide out of the home within the neighboring town. So yeah. Like I said, they would all look out for June and I appreciate it. But it was.
